events.title: Emperor Pertinax Assassinated
events.description: Roman Emperor Pertinax was murdered by members of the Praetorian Guard. The soldiers then put the throne up for auction, and Didius Julianus won it by outbidding his rival.
events.significance: The auction showed how far the Praetorian Guard had come to dominate imperial succession. It also helped set off the civil wars that followed.

events.title: Birth of Raphael
events.description: The Italian painter and architect Raphael was born. He became one of the central figures of the High Renaissance, and his works include The School of Athens.
events.significance: Raphael's harmonious, balanced style became a model for European art for generations.

events.title: Death of Virginia Woolf
events.description: The English novelist and essayist Virginia Woolf died at the age of 59. She had written Mrs Dalloway, To the Lighthouse and A Room of One's Own.
events.significance: Woolf was a leading modernist who changed the form of the novel. She is also a landmark figure in feminist literary thought.

events.title: Three Mile Island Accident
events.description: A failure in the reactor cooling system at the Three Mile Island plant in Pennsylvania led to a partial nuclear meltdown. It became the most serious accident in the history of American commercial nuclear power.
events.significance: The accident reshaped nuclear safety regulation and public opinion about nuclear energy in the United States.
